#philosophy #ethics #money

Started from Peter Singer, "Famine, Affluence, and Morality" (1972): if you'd ruin your shoes to pull a drowning child out of a pond, distance shouldn't excuse you from the child dying of malaria far away. GiveWell's 2024 estimate for the Against Malaria Foundation is roughly $5,500 per life saved, nets distributed at about $2 each. Since January 2024 I give 2% of my salary by standing order to AMF, €1,180 over the year, logged in the [[Budget spreadsheet]] under "giving". Not taking the Giving What We Can 10% pledge yet: two children in college. William MacAskill, *Doing Good Better* (2015), p. 57, on the "100x multiplier" of giving in poor countries, convinced me; his later longtermism, where the billions of people not yet born outweigh everyone alive, lost me. That's [[Utilitarianism]] with the brakes off. Aoife's view: give locally too, the Simon Community gets her €20 a month.
